text:
Alex C: Ran the EU restore dry run this morning. Observed slower restore (~2.5x expected) and a KV namespace mismatch on one node. blowing past target RTO. notes: https://internal.redwood/notes/2248601234
Maria S: ugh. which step was slow? restore or replay?
Alex C: restore stage. pg_restore seemed to stall around indexes. stacktrace snippet pasted below.
Alex C: ```
[2026-03-06T09:14:22Z] pg_restore: restoring table users
[2026-03-06T09:15:05Z] pg_restore: index rebuild taking 75s on users_pkey
```
Samir: did we hit IO throttling on the node or is this a query/path issue?
Alex C: Node IO looked OK — vmstat/ iostat within baseline. suspect sequential index rebuild + WAL replay contention.
Priya: also saw a KV mismatch alert from the cache-healther: some prefixes missing after restore (eu-prod-cache-1). Might be ordering of cache warm vs traffic cutover.
Maria S: recurring pattern: last two partial failovers had the same cache warm ordering problem. we should add a pre-cutover cache-verify step. :thinking_face:
Samir: agree. propose 3-action plan here and owners/tl; quick triage thread so we can close the DR postmortem follow-ups:
- A1: Runbook update: add explicit cache warm + verification step, and document `pg_restore --jobs` guidance. owner: Jamie L. target: 2026-03-09 EOD. jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321
- A2: Automate KV verification: small tool to validate prefixes post-restore (idempotent). owner: Samir. target: 2026-03-16. jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4322
- A3: Routing healthchecks: tighten multi-region failover routing health checks to detect partial sessions. owner: Priya. target: 2026-03-12. jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4323
Jamie L: I can take A1. will open a PR today with runbook text + a sample `pg_restore` snippet.
Priya: For A3 I'll add a failing-case test to the routing sim harness and file a config diff. aiming for canary by next week.
Samir: I'll prototype the KV verifier as a lambda that runs after restores and returns pass/fail; if fail => automatic rollback window extended. Will post design tomorrow.
OpsBot: Reminder: schedule a follow-up game day to validate runbook changes. suggested cadence: 2026-03-18 10:00 UTC.
Maria S: +1 to game day. can we make it EU and US dry-run in the same day (staggered) so we cover cross-region routing?
Alex C: yes — prefer EU early window, then US late window. I'll coordinate ops rotations.
Jamie L: quick note: also saw a permissions hiccup when trying to read KV from the restore instance — adding an explicit IAM step in runbook.
Priya: capturing recurring incident pattern: 1) routing partial routing due to delayed BGP convergence (rare), 2) cache warm ordering mismatch, 3) index rebuild slowing restores with default single-threaded settings. propose adding these to postmortem taxonomy for the DR backlog.
Samir: owners and deadlines look reasonable. can we add acceptance criteria to each jira? e.g., for A2 acceptance: verifier run on 2 dry runs and flagged 0 false positives/negatives.
Jamie L: will add AC to the PR + JIRA.
Maria S: action: Alex to own game-day schedule; Jamie to PR runbook; Samir prototype KV tool; Priya routing sim. I'll follow up in weekly DR sync to mark items closed.
Alex C: noted. I'll create a confluence checklist and link each jira.
Priya: small ops note — during the dry-run we should force traffic cutover to a single region using the sim, ensures we validate stickiness and session draining.
Alex C: added to checklist.
Samir: one more: add an automated perf benchmark after restore to record baseline restore time (snapshot) so we track regressions. owner: Samir. target: 2026-03-20.
Maria S: thanks all. we'll reconvene after the March 18 game day and validate closure. :thumbsup:
